title: US and Iran continue to trade strikes. Tehran hits US bases in Jordan.
body: The immediate market focus is oil, given direct strikes on tanker traffic and explicit Iranian threats to shipping around the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports that host the US military. Any rerouting or suspension of transits through that corridor would tighten freight and insurance costs and add a fresh geopolitical risk premium to crude benchmarks. Iran's warning against US-linked tankers, paired with Washington's pledge to keep targeting Iranian tankers in response to attacks on US Navy assets, points to sustained rather than one-off disruption risk. With the missile exchange marking one of the largest waves in months and both sides signalling further escalation, oil traders are likely to keep a heavy risk premium priced in through coming sessions. --- Earlier: Several explosions heard on Kharg Island - report A tanker war has turned into open strikes on military bases, with Iran and the US now trading direct hits and explicit threats to Gulf shipping.

title: Chile Central Bank Holds Key Rate at 4.5%
body: Chile's central bank unanimously left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 4.5% in September, pointing to elevated uncertainty stemming from the conflict in the Middle East, rising oil prices, and persistent global inflation risks. Oil prices have moved close to $100 per barrel, while copper has risen above $6.50 per pound. On the domestic front, economic activity remained weaker than anticipated in the second quarter and at the start of the third, with a slowdown in internal demand, job losses, and a higher unemployment rate. Headline inflation rose to 4.1% in August, mainly due to more volatile components, while core inflation remained stable at 3.3%. Inflation expectations over a two‑year horizon continue to be anchored at 3%. The central bank reiterated that monetary policy decisions will be made on a meeting‑by‑meeting basis. It emphasized that risks associated with the international conflict and the possibility of a more prolonged domestic slowdown warrant particularly close monitoring. title: El Salvador Inflation Picks Up in August
body: Annual inflation in El Salvador rose to 3.19% in August 2026, up from 2.49% in July, marking the highest rate since July 2023. Price growth accelerated in several categories, including food and non-alcoholic beverages (3.65% vs 2.49%), alcoholic beverages and tobacco (2.62% vs 2.11%), health (0.54% vs 0.39%), transport (2.91% vs 2.57%), communications (8.23% vs 4.95%), and miscellaneous goods and services (2.14% vs 1.96%). Inflation also picked up for clothing and footwear, rising to 2.62% from 2.11%. In contrast, inflation eased in the education sector (3.30% vs 3.65%). Deflation was recorded in housing and utilities (-0.32% vs 0.05%) and in recreation and culture (-0.91% vs -0.90%). Price growth for furniture and household goods held steady at 1.90%, while prices in restaurants and hotels were unchanged, resulting in a flat inflation rate for that category. title: Chile Holds Benchmark Rate at 4.50% in September, Extending Pause in Easing Cycle
body: Chile's central bank kept its key interest rate unchanged at 4.50% in its September 2026 decision, maintaining the same level set at its previous meeting in July 2026. The move confirms a continued pause in the bank's rate-cutting cycle, signaling a wait-and-see approach as policymakers monitor inflation dynamics and broader economic conditions. By holding the benchmark rate steady at 4.50%, the central bank leaves borrowing costs unchanged for households and businesses for at least another meeting. The decision suggests that authorities may be seeking more evidence on price stability and growth trends before deciding on any further monetary adjustments. The latest update, dated 8 September 2026, indicates that the policy stance remains on hold, with markets likely to focus on upcoming inflation readings and economic data for clues on the timing and direction of the next rate move. title: Ibovespa Rises With Broad Gains
body: The Ibovespa advanced 1.2% on Tuesday, closing at 187,367 points in a broad-based rally following Monday's holiday. Petrobras climbed 2.1% as oil prices jumped after attacks on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East. Banks also outperformed: Bradesco gained 1.8% and Itaú rose 1.2%, supported by the latest Focus survey, which projected lower inflation and reinforced expectations of further interest-rate cuts. On the political front, a BTG/Nexus poll indicated a technical tie in a potential presidential runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula, with Flávio holding a narrow one-point lead. A Quaest poll released on Monday likewise showed both candidates tied at 41% in a second-round scenario. Markets tend to view Flávio Bolsonaro as more fiscally conservative, a stance that resonates in an environment of elevated yields and weak business activity. In corporate news, Sabesp added 1.1% after several brokerages raised their price targets on the stock following a meeting with the company's management. title: TSX Falls on Broad Losses
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index declined 1.1% to close at 36,123, weighed down by weakness in financial, industrial, and technology stocks. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect, covering $20 billion worth of imports, with duties ranging from 15% to 50% on products including steel, furniture, clothing, and electronics. The US tariffs introduced last month targeted $20 billion of Canadian exports, equivalent to about 5% of total shipments to the United States. President Trump said Monday that Bombardier (-1.5%) would not be allowed to sell planes in the US unless it began manufacturing there. Financials also came under pressure as oil prices rose amid an escalation in the US–Iran war, stoking concerns about potential energy supply disruptions and inflation and strengthening expectations for further interest rate hikes. Royal Bank of Canada fell 1.1%, and TD Bank declined 1.2%. Technology stocks mirrored weakness in US hyperscalers and other credit‑sensitive software names, with Shopify tumbling 7.8% and Constellation Software sliding 5.6%. Enbridge gained 0.5% after announcing that CEO Greg Ebel will retire by late 2026 and be succeeded by Michele Harradence. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Crude Oil Hits Six-Week High
body: Crude oil rose back to $94 a barrel on Tuesday, its highest level in six weeks, driven by mounting fears of supply disruptions. The US military struck targets near Kharg Island and the port city of Jask, including Iranian oil tankers. Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, handles about 90% of the country's crude loadings. Saudi Aramco facilities came under fresh attack on Monday, with Iran-backed Houthi militants claiming responsibility for strikes on the 400,000-barrel-a-day Jazan refinery and other installations serving the domestic market. On Saturday, the US military hit three Iranian oil tankers after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships. Further supporting prices, Iran announced on Monday that it will set up a new shipping corridor with Oman in the Strait of Hormuz. Under the plan, vessels would be required to coordinate with Tehran before entering a newly designated restricted maritime zone around the key waterway. title: US Stocks Fall Amid Rising Energy Prices
body: US stock indices finished lower on Tuesday as rising energy prices pressured the outlook for corporate profit margins and heightened the risk of further interest-rate increases. Investors also remained cautious ahead of key inflation data due later this week. The S&P 500 declined 0.6%, the Nasdaq slipped 0.3%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 628 points. Geopolitical tensions added to market nerves. Fresh strikes involving the US and Iran intensified worries about prolonged disruptions to fuel exports from the Persian Gulf, while Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure curtailed the country's production capacity. Financing conditions for US companies tightened as well. Yields moved higher following hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan and expectations that Japanese authorities may sell US Treasuries to support the yen. Higher borrowing costs weighed particularly on credit‑sensitive software names: Microsoft dropped 1.1%, Palantir slid 2.3%, and Amazon eased 0.6% ahead of its planned sterling‑denominated bond issuance. AI-focused companies have increasingly tapped foreign‑currency debt markets as US dollar bond issuance swells on the back of AI‑related financing needs. Against this backdrop, Oracle bucked the broader tech weakness, rising 2.4% ahead of its earnings report later this week. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
